SCENE: _Central office of the factory of Rossum’s Universal Robots.

The windows on the back wall look out on
SCENE: _Central office of the factory of Rossum’s Universal Robots.
Entrance R. down Right.
The windows on the back wall look out on the endless roads of factory buildings.
Door L. down Left.
On the Left wall large maps showing steamship and railroad routes.
On the Right wall are fastened printed placards.
(“Robots cheapest Labor,” etc.) In contrast to these wall fittings, the floor is covered with splendid Turkish carpet, a couch R.C.
A book shelf containing bottles of wine and spirits, instead of books._ _DOMIN is sitting at his desk at Left, dictating.
SULLA is at the typewriter upstage against the wall.
There is a leather couch with arms Right Center.
At the extreme Right an armchair.
At extreme Left a chair.
There is also a chair in front of DOMIN’S desk.
Two green cabinets across the upstage corners of the room complete the furniture.
DOMIN’S desk is placed up and down stage facing Right._ _Seen through the windows which run to the heights of the room are rows of factory chimneys, telegraph poles and wires.
There is a general passageway or hallway upstage at the Right Center which leads to the warehouse.
The ROBOTS are brought into the office through this entrance._ DOMIN.
(_Dictating_) Ready?
Sulla: Yes.
Domin: To E. M. McVicker & Co., Southampton, England.
Domin: “We undertake no guarantee for goods damaged in transit.

Domin: As soon as the consignment was taken on board we drew your captain’s attention to the fact that the vessel was unsuitable for the transportation of Robots; and we are therefore not responsible for spoiled freight.
Domin: We beg to remain, for Rossum’s Universal Robots, yours truly.”
Domin: (_SULLA types the lines._) Ready?
Sulla: Yes.
Domin: Another letter.
Domin: To the E. B. Huysen Agency, New York, U.S.A.
Domin: “We beg to acknowledge receipt of order for five thousand Robots.
Domin: As you are sending your own vessel, please dispatch as cargo equal quantities of soft and hard coal for R.U.R., the same to be credited as part payment (_BUZZER_) of the amount due us.”
Domin: (_Answering phone_) Hello!
Domin: This is the central office.
Domin: Yes, certainly.
Domin: Well, send them a wire.
Domin: Good. (_Rises_) “We beg to remain, for Rossum’s Universal Robots, yours very truly.”
Domin: Ready? SULLA.
Domin: Yes. DOMIN.
Domin: (_Answering small portable phone_) Hello!
Domin: Yes. No.
Domin: All right.
Domin: (_Standing back of desk, punching plug machine and buttons_) Another letter.
Domin: Freidrichswerks, Hamburg, Germany.
Domin: “We beg to acknowledge receipt of order for fifteen thousand Robots.”
Domin: (_Enter MARIUS R._) Well, what is it?
Marius: There’s a lady, sir, asking to see you.
Domin: A lady?
Domin: Who is she?
Marius: I don’t know, sir.
Marius: She brings this card of introduction.
Domin: (_Reading card_) Ah, from President Glory.
Domin: Ask her to come in-- (_To SULLA.
Domin: Crossing up to her desk, then back to his own_) Where did I leave off?
Sulla: “We beg to acknowledge receipt of order for fifteen thousand Robots.”
Domin: Fifteen thousand.
Domin: Fifteen thousand.
Marius: (_At door R._) Please step this way.
(_Enter HELENA.
Marius: Exit MARIUS R._) HELENA.
Marius: (_Crossing to desk_) How do you do?
Domin: How do you do?
Domin: What can I do for you?
Helena: You are Mr. Domin, the General Manager?
Domin: I am.
Helena: I have come-DOMIN.
Helena: With President Glory’s card.
Helena: That is quite sufficient.
Helena: President Glory is my father.
Helena: I am Helena Glory.
Domin: Please sit down.
Domin: Sulla, you may go.
Domin: (_Exit SULLA L. Sitting down L. of desk_) How can I be of service to you, Miss Glory?
Helena: I have come-- (_Sits R. of desk._) DOMIN.
Helena: To have a look at our famous works where people are manufactured.
Helena: Like all visitors.
Helena: Well, there is no objection.
Helena: I thought it was forbidden to-DOMIN.
Helena: To enter the factory?
Helena: Yes, of course.
Helena: Everybody comes here with someone’s visiting card, Miss Glory.
Helena: And you show them-DOMIN.
Helena: Only certain things.
Helena: The manufacture of artificial people is a secret process.
Helena: If you only knew how enormously that-DOMIN.
Helena: Interests you.
Helena: Europe’s talking about nothing else.
Helena: (_Indignantly turning front_) Why don’t you let me finish speaking?
Domin: (_Drier_) I beg your pardon.
Domin: Did you want to say something different?
Helena: I only wanted to ask-DOMIN.
Helena: Whether I could make a special exception in your case and show you our factory.
Helena: Why, certainly, Miss Glory.
Helena: How do you know I wanted to say that?
Domin: They all do.
Domin: But we shall consider it a special honor to show you more than we do the rest.
Helena: Thank you.
Domin: (_Standing_) But you must agree not to divulge the least-HELENA.
Domin: (_Standing and giving him her hand_) My word of honor.
Domin: Thank you.
Domin: (_Looking at her hand_) Won’t you raise your veil?
Helena: Of course.
Helena: You want to see whether I’m a spy or not--I beg your pardon.
Domin: (_Leaning forward_) What is it?
Helena: Would you mind releasing my hand?
Domin: (_Releasing it_) Oh, I beg _your_ pardon.
Helena: (_Raising veil_) How cautious you have to be here, don’t you?
Domin: (_Observing her with deep interest_) Why, yes.
Domin: Hm--of course--We--that is-HELENA.
Domin: But what is it?
Domin: What’s the matter?
Domin: I’m remarkably pleased.
Domin: Did you have a pleasant crossing?
Helena: Yes.
Domin: No difficulty?
Helena: Why?
Domin: What I mean to say is--you’re so _young_.
Helena: May we go straight into the factory?
Domin: Yes.
Domin: Twenty-two, I think.
Helena: Twenty-two what?
Domin: Years.
Helena: Twenty-one.
Helena: Why do you want to know?
Domin: Well, because--as-- (_Sits on desk nearer her_) You will make a long stay, won’t you?
Helena: (_Backing away R._) That depends on how much of the factory you show me.
Domin: (_Rises; crosses to her_) Oh, hang the factory.
Domin: Oh, no, no, you shall see everything, Miss Glory.
Domin: Indeed you shall.
Domin: Won’t you sit down?
(_Takes her to couch R.C.
She sits.
Offers her cigarette from case at end of sofa.
Domin: She refuses._) HELENA.
Domin: Thank you.
Domin: But first would you like to hear the story of the invention?
Helena: Yes, indeed.

Domin: (_Crosses to L.C. near desk_) It was in the year 1920 that old Rossum, the great physiologist, who was then quite a young scientist, took himself to the distant island for the purpose of studying the ocean fauna.

Domin: (_She is amused._) On this occasion he attempted by chemical synthesis to imitate the living matter known as protoplasm until he suddenly discovered a substance which behaved exactly like living matter although its chemical composition was different.
Domin: That was in the year 1932, exactly four hundred and forty years after the discovery of America.
Domin: Whew-HELENA.
Domin: Do you know that by heart?
Domin: (_Takes flowers from desk to her_) Yes.
Domin: You see, physiology is not in my line.
Domin: Shall I go on?
Helena: (_Smelling flowers_) Yes, please.
Domin: (_Center_) And then, Miss Glory, Old Rossum wrote the following among his chemical experiments: “Nature has found only one method of organizing living matter.
Domin: There is, however, another method, more simple, flexible and rapid which has not yet occurred to Nature at all.
Domin: This second process by which life can be developed was discovered by me today.”
Domin: Now imagine him, Miss Glory, writing those wonderful words over some colloidal mess that a dog wouldn’t look at.

Domin: Imagine him sitting over a test tube and thinking how the whole tree of life would grow from him, how all animals would proceed from it, beginning with some sort of a beetle and ending with a _man_.
Domin: A man of different substance from us.
Domin: Miss Glory, that was a tremendous moment.
(_Gets box of candy from desk and passes it to her._)
Helena: Well-DOMIN.
Helena: (_As she speaks his portable PHONE lights up and he answers_) Well--Hello!--Yes--no, I’m in conference.
Helena: Don’t disturb me.
Helena: Well?

Domin: (_Smile_) Now, the thing was how to get the life _out_ of the test tubes, and hasten development and form organs, bones and nerves, and so on, and find such substances as catalytics, enzymes, hormones in short--you understand?
Helena: Not much, I’m afraid.
Domin: Never mind.
Domin: (_Leans over couch and fixes cushion for her back_) There!
Domin: You see with the help of his tinctures he could make whatever he wanted.
Domin: He could have produced a Medusa with the brain of Socrates or a worm fifty yards long-- (_She laughs.
Domin: He does also; leans closer on couch, then straightens up again_) --but being without a grain of humor, he took into his head to make a vertebrate or perhaps a man.
Domin: This artificial living _matter_ of his had a raging thirst for life.
Domin: It didn’t mind being sown or mixed together.
Domin: That couldn’t be done with natural albumen.
Domin: And that’s how he set about it.
Helena: About what?
Domin: About imitating Nature.
Domin: First of all he tried making an artificial dog.
Domin: That took him several years and resulted in a sort of stunted calf which _died_ in a few days.
Domin: I’ll show it to you in the museum.
Domin: And _then_ old Rossum started on the manufacture of _man_.
Helena: And I’m to divulge this to nobody?
Domin: To nobody in the world.
Helena: What a pity that it’s to be discovered in _all_ the school books of both Europe and America.
(_BOTH laugh._)
Domin: Yes. But do you know what _isn’t_ in the school books?
Domin: That old Rossum was mad.
Domin: Seriously, Miss Glory, you must keep this to yourself.
Domin: The old crank wanted to actually make _people_.
Helena: But you do make people.
Domin: _Approximately_--Miss Glory.
Domin: But old Rossum meant it literally.
Domin: He wanted to become a sort of scientific substitute for _God_.
Domin: He was a fearful materialist, and that’s why he did it all.
Domin: His sole purpose was nothing more or less than to prove that God was no longer necessary.
Domin: (_Crosses to end of couch_) Do you know anything about anatomy?
Helena: Very little.
Domin: Neither do I. Well-- (_He laughs_) --he then decided to manufacture everything as in the human body.
Domin: I’ll show you in the museum the bungling attempt it took him ten years to produce.
Domin: It was to have been a _man_, but it lived for three days only.
Domin: Then up came _young_ Rossum, an engineer.
Domin: He was a wonderful fellow, Miss Glory.
Domin: When he saw what a mess of it the old man was making he said: “It’s absurd to spend ten years making a man.
Domin: If you can’t make him quicker than Nature, you might as well shut up shop.”
Domin: Then he set about learning anatomy himself.
Helena: There’s nothing about _that_ in the school books?
Domin: No.
Domin: The school books are full of paid advertisements, and rubbish at that.
Domin: What the school books say about the _united efforts_ of the two great Rossums is all a fairy tale.
Domin: They used to have dreadful rows.

Domin: The old _atheist_ hadn’t the slightest conception of industrial _matters_, and the end of it was that Young Rossum shut him up in some laboratory or other and let him fritter the time away with his monstrosities while he himself started on the business from an _engineer’s_ point of view.
Domin: Old Rossum _cursed_ him and before he died he managed to botch up two physiological horrors.
Domin: Then one day they found him dead in the _laboratory_.
Domin: And that’s his whole story.
Helena: And what about the young man?
Domin: (_Sits beside her on couch_) Well, anyone who has looked into human anatomy will have seen at once that man is too complicated, and that a good engineer could make him more simply.
Domin: So young Rossum began to _overhaul_ anatomy to see what could be left out or simplified.
Domin: In short--But this isn’t boring you, Miss Glory?
Helena: No, indeed.
Helena: You’re--It’s awfully interesting.

Domin: (_Gets closer_) So young Rossum said to himself: “A man is something that feels happy, plays the piano, likes going for a walk, and, in fact, wants to do a whole lot of things that are really unnecessary.”
Domin: That are unnecessary when he wants-- (_Takes her hand_) --let us say, to weave or count.
Domin: Do you play the piano?
Helena: Yes.
Domin: That’s good.
(_Kisses her hand.
Domin: She lowers her head._) Oh, I beg your pardon!
Domin: (_Rises_) But a working machine must _not_ play the piano, must not feel happy, must not do a whole lot of other things.
Domin: A gasoline motor must not have tassels or ornaments, Miss Glory.
Domin: And to manufacture artificial workers is the same thing as the manufacture of a gasoline motor.
Domin: (_She is not interested._) The process must be the simplest, and the product the best from a practical point of view.
Domin: (_Sits beside her again_) What sort of worker do you think is the _best_ from a practical point of view?
Helena: (_Absently_) What?
(_Looks at him._)
Domin: What sort of worker do you think is the best from a practical point of view?
Helena: (_Pulling herself together_) Oh!
Helena: Perhaps the one who is most honest and hard-working.
Domin: No.
Domin: The one that is the _cheapest_.
Domin: The one whose requirements are the _smallest_.
Domin: Young Rossum invented a worker with the minimum amount of requirements.
Domin: He had to simplify him.
Domin: He rejected everything that did not contribute directly to the progress of work.
Domin: Everything that makes man more expensive.
Domin: In fact he _rejected man_ and made the _Robot_.
Domin: My dear Miss Glory, the Robots are not people.
Domin: Mechanically they are more _perfect_ than we are; they have an enormously developed intelligence, but they have no soul.
(_Leans back._)
Helena: How do you know they have no soul?
Domin: Have you ever seen what a Robot looks like inside?
Domin: Very neat, very simple.
Domin: Really a beautiful piece of work.
Domin: Not much _in_ it, but everything in flawless order.
Domin: The product of an engineer _is_ technically at a higher pitch of perfection than a product of Nature.
Helena: But man is supposed to be the product of God.
Domin: All the worse.
Domin: God hasn’t the slightest notion of modern engineering.
Domin: Would you believe that young Rossum then proceeded to play at being God?
Helena: (_Awed_) How do you mean?
Domin: He began to manufacture Super-Robots.
Domin: Regular giants they were.
Domin: He tried to make them twelve feet tall.
Domin: But you wouldn’t believe what a failure they were.
Helena: A failure?
Domin: Yes.
Domin: For no reason at all their limbs used to keep snapping off.
Domin: “Evidently our planet is too small for giants.”
Domin: Now we only make Robots of normal size and of very high-class human finish.
Helena: (_Hands him flower; he puts it in button-hole_) I saw the first Robots at home.
Helena: The Town Council bought them for--I mean engaged them for work.
Domin: No. _Bought_ them, Miss Glory.
Domin: Robots are bought and sold.
Helena: These were employed as street-sweepers.
Helena: I saw them sweeping.
Helena: They were so strange and quiet.
Domin: (_Rises_) Rossum’s Universal Robot factory doesn’t produce a uniform brand of Robots.
Domin: We have Robots of _finer_ and _coarser_ grades.
Domin: The best will live about _twenty_ years.
(_Crosses to desk.
HELENA looks in her pocket mirror.
Domin: He pushes button on desk._) HELENA.
Domin: Then they die?
Domin: Yes, they get used up.
Domin: (_Enter MARIUS, R. DOMIN crosses to C._) Marius, bring in samples of the manual labor Robot.
Domin: (_Exit MARIUS R.C._) I’ll show you specimens of the two extremes.
Domin: This first grade is comparatively inexpensive and is made in vast quantities.
(_MARIUS re-enters R.C. with two manual labor ROBOTS.
MARIUS is L.C., ROBOTS R.C., DOMIN at desk.
MARIUS stands on tiptoes, touches head, feels arms, forehead of one of the ROBOTS.
Domin: They come to a mechanical standstill._) There you are, as powerful as a small tractor.
Domin: Guaranteed to have average intelligence.
Domin: That will do, Marius.
(_MARIUS exits R.C. with ROBOTS._)
Helena: They make me feel so strange.
(_Crosses to desk.
Domin: Rings_) Did you see my new typist?
Helena: I didn’t notice her.
(_Enter SULLA L. She crosses and stands C., facing HELENA, who is still sitting in the couch._)
Domin: Sulla, let Miss Glory see you.
(_Looks at DOMIN.
Helena: Rising, crosses a step to C._) So pleased to meet you.
Helena: (_Looks at DOMIN_) You must find it terribly dull in this out of the way spot, don’t you?
Sulla: I don’t know, Miss Glory.
Helena: Where do you come from?
Sulla: From the factory.
Helena: Oh, were you born there?
Sulla: I was _made_ there.
Helena: What?
(_Looks first at SULLA, then at DOMIN._)
Domin: (_To SULLA, laughing_) Sulla is a Robot, best grade.
Helena: Oh, I beg your pardon.
Domin: (_Crosses to SULLA_) Sulla isn’t angry.
Domin: See, Miss Glory, the kind of skin we make.
Domin: Feel her face.
(_Touches SULLA’S face._)
Helena: Oh, no, no.
Domin: (_Examining SULLA’S hand_) You wouldn’t know that she’s made of different material from us, would you?
Domin: Turn ’round, Sulla.
(_SULLA does so.
Domin: Circles twice._) HELENA.
Domin: Oh, stop, stop.
Domin: Talk to Miss Glory, Sulla.
(_Examines hair of SULLA._)
Sulla: Please sit down.
Sulla: (_HELENA sits on couch._) Did you have a pleasant crossing?
(_Fixes her hair._)
Helena: Oh, yes, certainly.
Sulla: Don’t go back on the _Amelia_, Miss Glory, the barometer is falling steadily.
Sulla: Wait for the _Pennsylvania_.
Sulla: That’s a good powerful vessel.
Domin: What’s its speed?
Sulla: Forty knots an hour.
Sulla: Fifty thousand tons.
Sulla: One of the latest vessels, Miss Glory.
Helena: Thank you.
Sulla: A crew of fifteen hundred, Captain Harpy, eight boilers-DOMIN.
Sulla: That’ll do, Sulla.
Sulla: Now show us your knowledge of French.
Helena: You know French?
Sulla: Oui!
Sulla: Madame! I know four languages.
Sulla: I can write: “Dear Sir, Monsieur, Geehrter Herr, Cteny pane.”
Helena: (_Jumping up, crosses to SULLA_) Oh, that’s absurd!
Helena: Sulla isn’t a Robot.
Helena: Sulla is a girl like me.
Helena: Sulla, this is outrageous--Why do you take part in such a hoax?
Sulla: I am a Robot.
Helena: No, no, you are not telling the truth.
Helena: (_She catches the amused expression on DOMIN’S face_) I know they have forced you to do it for an advertisement.
Helena: Sulla, you are a girl like me, aren’t you?
(_Looks at him._)
Domin: I’m sorry, Miss Glory. _Sulla is a Robot._ HELENA.
Domin: It’s a lie!
Domin: What?
Domin: (_Pushes button on desk_) Well, then I must _convince_ you.
(_Enter MARIUS R.C.
Domin: He stands just inside the door._) Marius, take Sulla into the dissecting room, and tell them to open her up at once.
(_MARIUS moves toward C._)
Helena: Where? DOMIN.
Helena: Into the dissecting room.
Helena: When they’ve _cut her open_, you can go and have a look.
(_MARIUS makes a start toward SULLA._)
Helena: (_Stopping MARIUS_) No!
Helena: No! DOMIN.
Helena: Excuse me, you spoke of lies.
Helena: You wouldn’t have her killed?
Domin: You can’t kill machines.
Domin: Sulla! (_MARIUS one step forward, one arm out.
Domin: SULLA makes a move toward R. door._) HELENA.
Domin: (_Moves a step R._) Don’t be afraid, Sulla.
Domin: I won’t let you go.
Domin: Tell me, my dear-- (_Takes her hand_) --are they always so cruel to you?
Domin: You mustn’t put up with it, Sulla.
Domin: You mustn’t.
Sulla: I am a Robot.
Helena: That doesn’t matter.
Helena: Robots are just as good as we are.
Helena: Sulla, you wouldn’t let yourself be cut to pieces?
Sulla: Yes.
(_Hand away._)
Helena: Oh, you’re not afraid of death, then?
Sulla: I cannot tell, Miss Glory.
Helena: Do you know what would happen to you in there?
Sulla: Yes, I should cease to move.
Helena: How dreadful!
(_Looks at SULLA._)
Domin: Marius, tell Miss Glory what you are?
(_Turns to HELENA._)
Marius: (_To HELENA_) Marius, the Robot.
Domin: Would you take Sulla into the dissecting room?
Marius: (_Turns to DOMIN_) Yes.
Domin: Would you be sorry for her?
Marius: (_Pause_) I cannot tell.
Domin: What would happen to her?
Marius: She would cease to move.
Marius: They would put her into the stamping mill.
Domin: That is death, Marius.
Domin: Aren’t you afraid of death?
Domin: You see, Miss Glory, the Robots have no interest in life.
Domin: They have no enjoyments.
Domin: They are _less_ than so much grass.
Helena: Oh, stop.
Helena: Please send them away.
Domin: (_Pushes button_) Marius, Sulla, you may go.
(_MARIUS pivots and exits R. SULLA exits L._)
Helena: How terrible!
Helena: (_To C._) It’s outrageous what you are doing.
(_He takes her hand._)
Domin: Why outrageous?
(_His hand over hers.
Domin: Laughing._) HELENA.
Domin: I don’t know, but it is.
Domin: Why do you call her “Sulla”?
Domin: Isn’t it a nice name?
(_Hand away._)
Helena: It’s a man’s name.
Helena: Sulla was a Roman General.
Domin: What!
Domin: Oh! (_Laughs_) We thought that Marius and Sulla were lovers.
Helena: (_Indignantly_) Marius and Sulla were generals and fought against each other in the year--I’ve forgotten now.
Domin: (_Laughing_) Come here to the window.
(_He goes to window C._)
Helena: What? DOMIN.
Helena: Come here.
Helena: (_She goes._) Do you see anything?
(_Takes her arm.
Helena: She is on his R._) HELENA.
Helena: Bricklayers.
Domin: Robots.
Domin: All our work people are Robots.
Domin: And down there, can you see anything?
Helena: Some sort of office.
Domin: A counting house.
Domin: And in it-HELENA.
Domin: A lot of officials.
Domin: Robots!
Domin: All our officials are Robots.
Domin: And when you see the factory-- (_Noon WHISTLE blows.
She is scared; puts arm on DOMIN.
Domin: He laughs_) If we don’t blow the whistle the Robots won’t stop working.
Domin: In two hours I’ll show you the kneading trough.
(_BOTH come down stage.
Domin: HELENA is L.C. and DOMIN is R.C., arm in arm._) HELENA.
Domin: Kneading trough?
Domin: The pestle for beating up the paste.
Domin: In each one we mix the ingredients for a thousand Robots at one operation.
Domin: Then there are the vats for the preparation of liver, brains, and so on.
Domin: Then you will see the bone factory.
Domin: After that I’ll show you the spinning mill.
Helena: Spinning mill?
Domin: Yes.
Domin: For weaving nerves and veins.
Domin: Miles and miles of digestive tubes pass through it at a time.
Helena: (_Watching his gestures_) Mayn’t we talk about something else?
Domin: Perhaps it would be better.
Domin: There’s only a _handful_ of us among a hundred thousand Robots, and _not one woman_.
Domin: We talk nothing but the factory _all_ day, and _every_ day.
Domin: It’s just as if we were under a curse, Miss Glory.
Helena: I’m _sorry_ I said that you were lying.
(_A KNOCK at door R._)
Domin: Come in.
(_He is C._) (_From R. enter DR. GALL, DR. FABRY, ALQUIST and DR. HALLEMEIER.
ALL act formal--conscious.
Domin: ALL click heels as introduced._) DR. GALL.
Domin: (_Noisily_) I beg your pardon.
Domin: I hope we don’t intrude.
Domin: No, no.
Domin: Come in.
Domin: Miss Glory, here are Gall, Fabry, Alquist, Hallemeier.
Domin: This is President Glory’s daughter.
(_ALL move to her and shake her hand._)
Helena: How do you do?
Fabry: We had no idea-DR. GALL.
Fabry: Highly honored, I’m sure-ALQUIST.
Fabry: Welcome, Miss Glory.
Busman: (_Rushes in from R._) Hello, what’s up?
Domin: Come in, Busman.
Domin: This is President Glory’s daughter.
Domin: This is Busman, Miss Glory.
Busman: By Jove, that’s fine.
(_ALL click heels.
Busman: He crowds in and shakes her hand_) Miss Glory, may we send a cablegram to the papers about your arrival?
Helena: No, no, please don’t.
Domin: Sit down, please, Miss Glory.
(_On the line, “Sit down, please,” all SIX MEN try to find her a chair at once.
HELENA goes for the chair at the extreme L. DOMIN takes the chair at front of desk, places it in the C. of stage.
HALLEMEIER gets chair at SULLA’S typewriter and places it to R. of chair at C. BUSMAN gets armchair from extreme R., but by now HELENA has sat in DOMIN’S preferred chair, at C. ALL sit except DOMIN.
BUSMAN at R. in armchair.
Domin: FABRY in swivel chair back of desk._) BUSMAN.
Domin: Allow me-DR. GALL.
Domin: Please-FABRY.
Domin: Excuse me-ALQUIST.
Domin: What sort of a crossing did you have?
Dr. Gall: Are you going to stay long?
(_MEN conscious of their appearance.
ALQUIST’S trousers turned up at bottom.
He turns them down.
BUSMAN polishes shoes.
Dr. Gall: OTHERS fix ties, collars, etc._) FABRY.
Dr. Gall: What do you think of the factory, Miss Glory?
Dr. Gall: Did you come over on the _Amelia_?
